actions.name: Conduct reconnaissance to gather victim identity information
actions.description: The actors likely conduct reconnaissance operations to gather victim identity information.

actions.name: Gain persistent access via brute force
actions.description: The actors gain persistent access to victim networks frequently via brute force.

actions.name: Use brute force password spraying to obtain valid user and group email account credentials
actions.description: The actors used password spraying to obtain valid user and group email account credentials, allowing them access to the network.

actions.name: Use valid accounts hosted on Microsoft 365, Azure, and Okta cloud environments for initial access
actions.description: The actors used accounts hosted on Microsoft 365, Azure, and Okta cloud environments as additional methods for initial access.

actions.name: Exploit Citrix external-facing remote services for initial access
actions.description: The actors exploited Citrix systems’ external-facing remote services as another method for gaining initial access to the system.

actions.name: Send MFA push notifications to legitimate users to gain access (MFA fatigue / push bombing)
actions.description: The actors send MFA requests to legitimate users seeking acceptance of the request, bombarding users with mobile phone push notifications until the user either approves the request by accident or stops the notifications.

actions.name: Register attacker devices with MFA using compromised user accounts
actions.description: The actors leveraged a compromised user’s open registration for MFA to register the actor’s own device to access the environment via the valid account.

actions.name: Use self-service password reset (SSPR) tool on public facing ADFS to reset expired passwords and register MFA
actions.description: The actors used a self-service password reset (SSPR) tool associated with a public facing Active Directory Federation Service (ADFS) to reset the accounts with expired passwords and then registered MFA through Okta for compromised accounts without MFA already enabled.

actions.name: Use VPN service for conducting activity
actions.description: The actors frequently conduct their activity using a virtual private network (VPN) service. Several of the IP addresses in the actors’ malicious activity originate from exit nodes tied to the Private Internet Access VPN service.

actions.name: Use Microsoft Word to open PowerShell to launch RDP binary mstsc.exe for lateral movement
actions.description: The actors used Microsoft Word to open PowerShell to launch the RDP binary mstsc.exe for lateral movement.

actions.name: Perform Kerberos Service Principal Name (SPN) enumeration and receive Kerberos tickets
actions.description: The actors performed Kerberos Service Principal Name (SPN) enumeration of several service accounts and received Kerberos tickets.

actions.name: Use Active Directory Microsoft Graph API PowerShell application to perform directory dump of all AD accounts
actions.description: The actors used the Active Directory (AD) Microsoft Graph Application Program Interface (API) PowerShell application likely to perform a directory dump of all AD accounts.

actions.name: Import DomainPasswordSpray.ps1 tool from GitHub to conduct password spraying
actions.description: The actors imported the tool DomainPasswordSpray.ps1, which is openly available on GitHub, likely to conduct password spraying.

actions.name: Use Cmdkey /list command to display usernames and credentials
actions.description: The actors used the command Cmdkey /list, likely to display usernames and credentials.

actions.name: Attempt impersonation of domain controller exploiting CVE-2020-1472 (Netlogon vulnerability)
actions.description: The actors attempted impersonation of the domain controller, likely by exploiting Microsoft’s Netlogon (also known as “Zerologon”) privilege escalation vulnerability (CVE-2020-1472).

actions.name: Use living off the land (LOTL) Windows command-line tools for discovery
actions.description: The actors leverage living off the land (LOTL) to gain knowledge about the target systems and internal networks using Windows command-line tools such as nltest and net group commands.

actions.name: Use LDAP query in PowerShell to search Active Directory for computer display names, OS, descriptions, and distinguished names
actions.description: The actors used an LDAP query in PowerShell to search the AD for computer display names, operating systems, descriptions, and distinguished names.

actions.name: Make outbound connections using msedge.exe likely to Cobalt Strike Beacon C2 infrastructure
actions.description: Using msedge.exe, the actors likely made outbound connections to Cobalt Strike Beacon command and control (C2) infrastructure.

actions.name: Download files related to remote access methods and organization’s inventory
actions.description: While logged in to victim accounts, the actors downloaded files related to gaining remote access to the organization and to the organization’s inventory, likely exfiltrating the files.
